reasons: The feasible covariance proof directly uses the influence-level identity proved in \(\text{prop:residual-cancellation}\), so that proposition must be an explicit dependency rather than only a transitive dependency through the parameter theorem.

narrow: The original uniform coverage clause includes local sequences for which \(\Omega_\theta\) collapses to zero. An explicit certificate is the scalar regular subproblem \(\sqrt N(\widehat b-b)=Z\), \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), with the smooth coordinate \(\Psi(b)=b^2\), plug-in covariance \(4\widehat b^2\), and \(b=2/\sqrt N\). At \(\alpha=0.05\), its limiting plug-in Wald coverage is \(\mathbb P\{|4Z+Z^2|\le2z_{0.975}|2+Z|\}\), approximately \(0.8765<0.95\), although the covariance estimator is consistent in absolute error and the pointwise first-order expansions hold. The same quadratic coordinate is embedded in the regular affine message family \(g_\beta(y,w)=y/2+w+\beta+\beta^2w\), whose additive \(\beta\) term retains mean rank and whose \(\beta^2w\) term gives the quadratic treatment contrast. Requiring the compact family to remain separated from the all-zero path covariance is therefore an honest scope restriction; the asymptotic linearity, Gaussian law, and covariance-consistency clauses remain unchanged.

verdict.note: Accepted added adaptive-linearization theorem and honest covariance-separation narrowing after high-effort mathematical adjudication; local quadratic counterexample verifies uniform zero-covariance failure.
